title: Personal priming and friction annotator — release notes
content:
Quick personal scratch — want to capture the micro experiments and friction I hit when trying the 8-bit quantized variant flip last week. Not a polished runbook, more of an annotated log + TODOs for next time.

Context:
- target: flip customer-facing route /v1/generate from model-v2 (fp16) -> model-v2-q8 (8-bit quant) as a slow canary.
- why: ~2.3x lower cost in perf tests; some tail latency regressions observed for cold sessions (KV cold misses).
- cadence: aim to do a soft 2% -> 10% -> 30% -> 100% over ~48–72h windows, but this needs priming adjustments.

High-level hypothesis:
- immediate perf regressions are driven by KV cache warmup and kernel selection thrash on first few hundred requests per worker. If we pre-prime (targeted short synthetic queries + small real cohorts) the cold penalty disappears.

Observed friction during last flip:
- cold-p95 spiked from 220ms -> 480ms for a small subset of tenants during 2% traffic window.
- token-cost savings visible immediately, but customer telemetry flagged doubled latency on interactive sessions.
- rollout automation (traffic-split) pushed some traffic to nodes without local primed KV (autoscaled new instances), causing re-introduced regressions even at 10% split.

Notes / small experiments to try next run (ordered):
1) Priming cohort (micro): pick 5 active tenants with high sessions and run synthetic priming (10 warm queries each) targeted at the same route immediately before switching them. Document who to call to approve "primed push" since this is risky.
2) Staggered instance warmup: when autoscaling creates a new worker, wait 30s for local kernel cache to stabilize then add to canary pool (delta from current 0s). See infra flag we can toggle: CANARY_ADD_DELAY_MS.
3) Client-aware sticky seeding: if SDK supports, bind a small set of client ids to the primed pool for first 5 requests. Reduces cross-cohort noise.
4) Small synthetic traffic generator: run a lightweight warmup using representative prompts (stored in /confluence/priming-prompts) at ~5rps per new instance.
5) Telemetry keys to watch: p50/p95/p99 latency per-tenant, kv-cache-hit-rate, kernel-switch-count, gpu-util, and token_cost_delta. Also count of autoscale events during window.

Quick checklist before flip (personal):
- [ ] Get signoff from Maya (latency ops) and Diego (infra autoscale tuning) — ping Slack thread and add to INF-2783.
- [ ] Create priming cohort list and note contact for each tenant.
- [ ] Validate CANARY_ADD_DELAY_MS toggle exists and test in staging.
- [ ] Generate priming traffic script and store as gh gist (link back in INF-2783).
- [ ] Add temporary dashboard widgets for the 48h window (per-tenant p95, kv hits, kernel-switches).
- [ ] Plan rollback TTL: if p95 > 2x baseline for >10m on >5% of primed tenants, revert.

Runbook sketch for operator (if I/we want to formalize):
- Phase 0 (prep, -24h): notify CS for tenants in cohort, create monitoring dashboard, set alert at p95 threshold, create canary config in infra.
- Phase 1 (soft 2%): enable priming for selected tenants (run script), wait 10m, sample telemetry for 20m, then flip traffic. Hold for 2h with increased watch.
- Phase 2 (10%): after 48h stable, expand to 10% with staggered add-delay and synthetic warmups for new instances.
- Phase 3 (30%): increase if stable for 24h.
- Phase full: run silent migration overnight with final small group priming and final cutover.
- Rollback: immediate traffic revert + trigger pre-recorded k8s image fallback (exact command in infra runbook) + notify CS.

Things I want to capture metrics-wise (notes to myself):
- baseline: compute tenant-level baseline p95 over previous 7 days for same wall-clock window. Use baseline for relative thresholds, not absolutes.
- sample-size: ensure at least 500 requests per-cohort within observation window to trust p95. If not enough traffic, treat as untestable — either pick different tenants or lengthen window.
- KV warmup curve: sample p95 across first 1000 requests and plot cumulative delta to baseline (helps tune priming count).

Edge cases I bumped into and quick mitigation ideas:
- autoscaler creates many small instances; priming all is expensive. Mitigation: limit scale-down aggressiveness for canary pool during window; require min-instances=2 for canary node pool.
- some tenants have weird prompt distributions (high seq length); priming using short prompts doesn't help. Mitigation: sample prompt lengths from prod traces and include long prompts in the synthetic priming set.
- kernel-swap oscillation when mixed fp16/q8 on same host. Mitigation: consider homogeneous host pools for quant variants (flagged in INF-2831).

Open questions / TODOs (personal):
- who owns changing CANARY_ADD_DELAY_MS in prod? need to add a quick owner and rollback path.
- can we record a short video demo of the priming script + dashboard to speed approvals? (Maya volunteered earlier).
- decide default priming size: 10 vs 30 queries. last flip 10 was borderline; 30 costy. need a small ab test.
- check if SDK-level sticky seeding is worth the added complexity.

Quick raw checklist for next trial (copyable to ticket):
- Prepare priming prompts (mix short/long) — owner: Aria
- Add CANARY_ADD_DELAY_MS test in staging — owner: Diego
- Create priming script GH gist & link — owner: Aria
- Dashboard widgets + alerts — owner: Maya
- CS heads up + tenant list — owner: product-eng

Notes to self (less formal):
- I should timestamp the priming runs carefully — humans kept starting priming while traffic flip in previous run which created overlapping noise.
- be conservative on scale-down during the first 24h. It will keep primed state alive.
- remind: include token-cost delta in postmortem. Ops tends to focus on latency only.

End of scratch. Keep this file lightweight; if we iterate and it looks stable, promote to shared drive /confluence as a short howto.

Last edit quick log:
- 2024-03-21: created initial notes after first flip (Aria)
- 2024-03-27: added staggered add-delay idea after sync with Diego
- 2024-04-12: added checklist and operator runbook sketch
- 2024-05-02: trimmed and prepared to copy into INF-2783 ticket
